name: nocobase-app-development
description: >-
  Primary entry for building complete NocoBase 3 applications and individual features:
  business and administration pages, routes, components, endpoints, data, permissions, services, translations, and tests.
  Use this application-local workflow instead of globally installed NocoBase 2
  Skills. For local or published NocoBase 3 plugin packages, use the project plugin development Skill.
metadata:
  short-description: Develop features in a NocoBase 3 application
---

# NocoBase 3 application development

When the task creates or maintains a plugin under this App's `packages/`, read `<app-root>/.agents/skills/nocobase-app-plugin-development/SKILL.md` by its explicit project path. It ships alongside this Skill in `@nocobase/app-skills`. Use this application's guidance for App-owned features and the plugin Skill for plugin-owned contracts and packaging; do not install the older global plugin development Skill.

Use this Skill when building a complete application or an individual feature: business and administration pages, endpoints, data, services and their tests.

For plugin-owned code, use the project plugin development Skill, whether the plugin stays local to this App or is published for reuse. Plugin development does not require a separate repository or a NocoBase source checkout.

Do not use it to upgrade the template this application was generated from, which is also how the application moves to a newer NocoBase version when the user asks to upgrade NocoBase or its core. That is `.agents/skills/nocobase-app-upgrade/`, which reconciles a newer template release against the application without reverting the user's work.

Check [browser API compatibility](references/frontend/frontend-dev.md#browser-api-compatibility) for direct calls and third-party integrations. HTTPS-only APIs require capability detection and a clear user-facing explanation when unavailable. UUID generation and copying text must support HTTP; use `createUuid()` and `copyText()` from `@nocobase/app-client`.

## Before you start

Read the application's `AGENTS.md` first for the rules that apply everywhere, and the `.agents/rules/` files its index points to for your task. This Skill's references are the detail behind it. Before running any `pnpm nocobase` command, read [the command line](references/cli.md): it maps tasks to commands and states the flags an agent must not add on its own.

Confirm you are in an application and not a plugin package. An application has:

```text
client/runtime.ts
server/runtime.ts
config.example.yml
```

If instead you find `client/plugin.ts`, `server/plugin.ts`, or a `defineServerPlugin()` declaration, you are in a plugin package and this Skill does not apply.

Do not infer the application's capabilities from a template name or from this Skill. Inspect `package.json`, `client/plugins.ts`, `server/plugins.ts`, `cli/plugins.ts`, `server/config/index.ts`, and `database/` before deciding what is installed, registered, configured, or application-owned. `nocobase.templatePackage` and `nocobase.templateKind` identify known template ancestry when present, but a new template remains valid without being listed here. Read [template variants](references/template-variants.md) only when those files identify one of the documented official templates.

## Plan the complete feature before implementation

For a new application or a feature spanning frontend and backend, identify the users' tasks, pages and key interactions together with the data, endpoint contracts and permissions before implementing either side. Read [the frontend workflow](references/frontend/ui-workflow.md#choosing-a-workflow) at this point, not only when opening `client/`. Reuse existing requirements, designs and installed capabilities; a routine CRUD feature can use a short implementation plan without a separate design document. Keep API-only, UI-only and other explicitly limited requests within their requested scope.

Proceed through the authorized implementation and verification without a routine design approval stop. Ask early only when a material business rule or scope decision cannot be resolved from the requirements, existing decisions and conventions, when work exceeds authorization, or when the user explicitly requested review first. State reasonable assumptions, preserve prior answers and continue unaffected work while a necessary decision is pending. Internal design and acceptance reviews are quality checks, not additional user approval rounds.

Deliver the requested user operation across its layers: pages invoke real endpoints, data is saved and refreshed correctly, permissions hold, and loading, empty and failure states are handled. Backend tests or a design document alone are progress, not completion of a full application. If the backend is already implemented, reuse and check its contracts against the required pages, close any gaps and finish the frontend without restarting design approval. Report missing implementation and unavailable verification explicitly.

## Choose where the feature belongs

For parent/child business flows, scoped references, single-person review or multi-step forms with private recoverable drafts, consult the [business example catalogue](references/business-examples.md) and its runnable scenario index. Its resources supplement the existing list/edit patterns; read each scenario's integration dependencies before adapting it.

Build application-specific features directly in the application by default. Use a plugin when the user requests one or when code reuse or modular organization calls for a separately registered, maintainable feature. Create local plugins under `packages/` with the project plugin development Skill; do not use the source repository's `packages/plugins/` layout. The App builds and packages registered local plugins for deployment without an npm release. Publish only when distributing the plugin through a package registry.

Ordinary internal workspace packages can share code without plugin registration. Follow [internal workspace packages](references/dependencies.md#internal-workspace-packages), keeping one application at the workspace root with internal packages under `packages/`. The [runnable package example](references/internal-package-example.md) supplies complete configuration and explains declaration watching.

## Check the installed plugins first

NocoBase packages may publish Skills under `.agents/skills/`. Current application templates run `pnpm nocobase skills sync` automatically through `postinstall`; run it manually if install scripts were disabled or that directory is missing or stale. Confirm that the package is a direct `@nocobase/*` dependency or a registered plugin before relying on its Skill. The common capability mappings are:

| The requirement sounds like                                    | Read the Skill for                                      |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Email, IM, or in-app messages                                  | `@nocobase/app-plugin-notification`                     |
| Knowledge bases, document spaces, search and document review   | `@nocobase/app-plugin-knowledge`                        |
| Approval processes, joint decisions and approval tasks         | `@nocobase/app-plugin-approval` (commercial Pro plugin) |
| Roles, permissions, per-user or per-record access              | `@nocobase/app-plugin-authorization`                    |
| Sign-in, registration, sessions                                | `@nocobase/app-plugin-authentication`                   |
| File upload and metadata through Repository                    | `@nocobase/app-plugin-file`                             |
| File storage, disk configuration, or custom drivers            | `@nocobase/drive`                                       |
| Translated text and language switching                         | `@nocobase/app-plugin-i18n`                             |
| User administration and application-owned role assignment      | `@nocobase/app-plugin-users`                            |
| Live updates, snapshot recovery and replacing business polling | `@nocobase/realtime` (`nocobase-realtime`)              |
| Reading or writing data, schema changes, migrations            | `@nocobase/db`                                          |

Read the relevant Skill before writing the feature, but treat this table as a map rather than an installed-package list. Implementing a permission system, a notification sender, or a scheduler by hand when a registered plugin provides one is the most expensive mistake available here.

For any required commercial NocoBase package, follow [commercial package access](references/plugins.md#commercial-package-access): automatically probe pkg-v3 with existing credentials, install a compatible authorized package without prompting, and leave a brief conversation notice for unavailable access while continuing independent work. This includes plugins and commercial database drivers; do not infer access to one package from another.

For knowledge base requirements, check `@nocobase/app-plugin-knowledge` first and follow [knowledge package integration](references/plugins.md#knowledge-base-integration). Apply the same automatic pkg-v3 access workflow when installation or update is needed. Read its synchronized Skill when available, otherwise its installed README, docs and public exports; do not assume it ships a Skill or build a substitute because one is absent.

For approval requirements, check `@nocobase/app-plugin-approval` first and follow [approval integration prerequisites](references/lifecycle.md#approval-requests-check-the-pro-plugin-first), then the plugin's installed Skill. Do not silently build a substitute approval engine from lifecycle examples. Simple single-person confirmation or rejection can remain lifecycle actions.

When the stages of a business record are fixed by developers rather than drawn by administrators — an expense report, a ticket, a contract, an order — build it with `@nocobase/lifecycle` as [record lifecycles](references/lifecycle.md) describes: the state stays in the record's own field and changes only through declared transitions. Declare only required business paths with precise sources and destinations; the diagram expands every `from × to` pair rather than analyzing routing logic. Follow [readable process graphs](references/lifecycle-ui.md#keep-process-graphs-readable) before rendering dense definitions.

For notification configuration or sending, follow the notification plugin Skill: `notification.channels` maps each name to one flat channel configuration with `type` (`provider` remains a compatibility alias), and `send({ idempotencyKey, messages })` supplies a complete message per Channel. Use native addresses; email and in-app arrays create independent deliveries, while Webhooks forbid `to`.

Install, update and customize plugins, and remove a direct NocoBase package, as [plugins](references/plugins.md) describes: `pnpm nocobase plugin register`, `plugin update` and `package remove` keep the manifest, the lockfile, the composition roots and the synchronized Skills consistent, so never hand-edit only one of them.

Business role assignments must be visible and editable through administration. Default to explicit users; do not assign application roles to every authenticated identity or broaden the inherited member role merely to enable a feature. Follow [permission assignment safety](references/authorization.md#visible-and-manageable-assignments) and run the template's initialized-assignment guard before delivery.

## Waiting feedback

For page/panel waits and native submit buttons, follow [pending feedback](references/pending-feedback.md). Use installed Loading/PendingButton and the shared timing hook; retain submission and list-state owners.

## Choose sample data or a demo system

A request to add example customers, orders or tasks normally means sample data in the existing application. Use `sample: true` seeds or `sampleDataToken`; see [sample data and demo systems](references/migrations.md#sample-data-and-demo-systems). Keep required initialization data in ordinary seeds. Do not infer an isolated demo deployment from the words "demo data" alone.

A dedicated demo system has its own database and storage, repeatable business-data generation/clear/reset, visitor write policies and optional simulated external or Agent execution. For that requirement, follow the `nocobase-app-plugin-demo-mode` Skill. If `@nocobase/app-plugin-demo-mode` is not yet a dependency, register it with `pnpm nocobase plugin register demo-mode`, which also synchronizes its Skill; the Skill exists in the application only after synchronization. The plugin supplies the environment mechanisms; the application supplies its dataset, cleanup, management UI and any simulation adapters. Sample data alone supplies none of those operating policies. Use the user's stated deployment and lifecycle requirements to choose; if the intended scope remains ambiguous, clarify it before adding full-business cleanup or changing the environment mode. A trial, staging or customer environment where users keep their data, a provider's sandbox credentials and an in-app presentation mode are not demo systems.

When the application already depends on `@nocobase/app-plugin-demo-mode`, a change that adds business collections, outbound integrations or background jobs also updates the demo dataset's cleanup and adapters; follow that Skill's maintenance section.

## Deliver system administration by default

When a user asks you to build a complete application, deliver the System settings structure ([System settings navigation](references/settings-navigation.md)) and administration pages alongside the business features, unless the user explicitly excludes them or requests a narrower deliverable such as an API-only service or a prototype explicitly limited to business screens. Users do not need to request administration pages individually. Include user management and role and permission management by default. Register workflow management, background tasks and other applicable administration as module cards of the System settings home; show execution status, failures and supported recovery actions within each capability's pages, without an additional Operational monitoring group. Reuse existing pages and installed plugins, and implement missing application-owned pages. Read [system administration](references/system-administration.md) for the baseline, capability-specific pages and acceptance criteria. For a focused feature change, extend existing administration where that feature requires it.

Whenever application requirements include a process to develop, deliver its workflow management pages by default, even when the user mentions only the business process. Reuse the installed `workflow-management` UI Library block, or install it with `yes n | pnpm exec shadcn add @nocobase/workflow-management`. Follow [Lifecycle UI](references/lifecycle-ui.md) for installation, application adapters and the default layout: one Workflow management settings card with in-page Definitions and Executions tabs, definition diagrams with visible parameter forms, and execution details with history and effects. The two tab views use URL-backed child routes without sidebar `navigation`. Extend an existing management area rather than adding a duplicate. Follow the scope exceptions in [system administration](references/system-administration.md#default-delivery).

For process management, distinguish administrator-adjustable reviewers, departments, thresholds and other [lifecycle parameters](references/lifecycle-parameters.md) from workflow structure, which remains defined in source unless a supported visual designer is explicitly required.

## Learn the endpoints from the API document

The running application describes every `/api` endpoint it serves — its own routes, every installed plugin's, the data endpoints and Better Auth's `/api/auth/...` — in an OpenAPI 3.1 document. Before calling an endpoint or building on one, fetch that document instead of reading route sources:

```bash
curl -H "x-api-key: <key>" http://127.0.0.1:13000/main/api/swagger
```

Replace `/main` with the application's `APP_BASE_PATH`. Swagger UI for people is at `<APP_BASE_PATH>/api/swagger/docs`. Reading either needs a signed-in session or an API key, which a signed-in user creates with `POST <APP_BASE_PATH>/api/apiKeys`; without one the routes answer `401`, and an application with no access check registered, such as one without the authentication plugin, answers `404`. Ask the user for a key rather than creating one yourself. [HTTP API design](references/http-api.md#api-documentation) explains how to read the document and how a new route declares itself in it.

## Include administration by default

For every application feature, apply [system settings delivery](references/system-settings.md) and place every administration surface in the [System settings navigation](references/settings-navigation.md) (one sidebar entry, a home of cards by category, tabs inside a module): keep unused business settings disabled in a newly created application while retaining its restricted App Foundation entry; as the application develops beyond that basic shell, reconcile the template's prepared Users and Roles and permissions routes and the management surfaces for each capability actually used. Inspect this on every build or iteration, enable missing routes once and preserve already enabled pages, including workflow definitions, diagrams, configuration and authorized execution history. When building process rules, proactively declare appropriate thresholds and reviewer choices as validated, authorized business parameters and provide visible parameter forms in workflow management, with optional diagram-bound shortcuts to the same editor; the user need not ask for configurability. Apply the same check to non-workflow business policy, mutable dictionaries, business document numbering, important operation records and the other used capabilities in that reference. Follow its [business administration recipes](references/business-administration.md) for application-owned implementations and acceptance. The real execution must consume the saved values; source/deployment configuration retains its owner. This is part of implementing the feature, not a separate user request.

For initialization prerequisites introduced by the feature, apply [setup readiness](references/setup-readiness.md): wire real required-role membership and applicable business relationship checks with the standard contextual hint. Users should see what configuration is missing and an authorized path to fix it. Installed plugins, read failures and missing business configuration are different states; keep the bare app and its protected App Foundation entry unchanged.

## Frontend work

Before implementing interactions, follow [component selection and source review](references/frontend/component-selection.md): existing business component → installed shadcn primitive → registry addition → justified custom composition/primitive. Record the actual component source and run the targeted component checker before delivery; a matching screenshot alone does not justify duplicating a primitive. A date field follows [Dates](references/frontend/references/form.md#dates): read the matching official shadcn Date Picker example, reuse or compose `client/components/date-picker.tsx` once, reuse it on every page, then run the checker and the field's behavior tests; a native or shadcn `Input` date input is never a date picker.

Application and plugin UI share [the UI design contract](references/frontend/design-contract.md). Read the application's existing design records and original UI references first: record whether a reference controls appearance, structure or style, apply authorized page exceptions, and retain reusable decisions outside synchronized Skills. Use the contract's system-design section when planning a business system across modules; do not redesign the system for a small edit. Plugin implementation still belongs to `nocobase-app-plugin-development`, whose UI entry points to these same design and acceptance rules.

For business lists, reuse the template-provided `DataTable` and companions from `#components/data-table`, backed by the supported TanStack Table v8 dependency. Use its controlled manual mode for server paging/sorting. Do not replace it with an agent-written table engine when a dependency version is incompatible; inspect and repair the dependency first. See [tables](references/frontend/references/table.md).

Every page and overlay you build or change works on a phone in the first delivery, without the user asking: decide its phone layout while designing it and verify it at phone widths before calling it done, following [the phone experience](references/frontend/mobile.md). Shrinking the desktop page, wrapping its toolbar or scrolling an ordinary table sideways does not count; ordinary lists use `DataTable`'s phone cards (`renderCard`) and its `search`, `filters` and `getColumnLabel` toolbar row, and create and edit forms sit in a `FeedbackForm` given `values={form.getValues}` and `savedValues` (the stored record, or the blank values; never the restored draft) inside the route overlay, which asks before discarding any difference on every way out, whatever changed it and with or without a saved draft.

**Table row actions are one "⋮" menu (T1.5, Must).** Every table row's actions, a single action included, render through `RowActions` from `#components/row-actions` at the end of the row: the same icon-only "⋮" trigger on every row, in every record state and on every page, business and administration lists alike, with no visible header text over the actions column and no sticky or right-pinned column. The record's state and the viewer's permissions change which items the menu holds, never how the entry looks; no item left means no menu. Never show an action as a text link, an outline button or a row of buttons because it seems frequent or primary: show a named action outside the menu (`exposed`) only when the user asked for it or a confirmed page design shows it, and pin the column only for a wide table whose actions are otherwise out of reach, recording the reason. Details: [section 8 of `table.md`](references/frontend/references/table.md#8-column-definitions-and-row-actions).

**Unsaved input is never lost silently (M7.4, Must).** Every create or edit form is a `FeedbackForm` from `#components/feedback-form` with `values={form.getValues}` and `savedValues` (the stored record as the form shows it, or the blank values of a new record; never the restored draft), rendered inside its `RouteDialog`, `RouteDrawer` or covering `RouteChildPage`; a form kept in `useState` instead of React Hook Form passes `values={() => values}` and `savedValues` the same way. That layer then asks "Discard changes?" before Cancel, ×, Esc, the backdrop, browser back and links, and the browser warns before a reload, whenever the form differs from what is saved. Keeping a draft does not replace the question, and neither does working storage: do not swap `FeedbackForm` for a plain `<form>`, do not make `dirty` or a `beforeunload` handler depend on a draft or storage state, do not render `OwnDiscardQuestion` because a draft is kept (it only declares that the file's own guard asks about its unsaved input, as the settings forms do; a guard that only blocks while a save runs asks nothing), and do not test "cancel, reopen, the input is back" as the cancel path. An unknown outcome is not a lock: after a lost response, a 5xx or a timeout, `submission.pending` stays true for the same-key retry, but only `submitting` blocks leaving. Cancel stays enabled, `beforeClose` and any guard of your own read only the save in flight (never `submission.pending`), and the `FeedbackForm`'s `values` and `savedValues` make every way out ask "Discard changes?" as before the save; "Keep editing" keeps the input for the retry, and "Discard" really leaves, with the key left in session storage so reopening offers the same retry. The [component checker](scripts/check-ui-components.mjs) rejects a plain create or edit `<form>`, a `FeedbackForm` without `values` and `savedValues` (React Hook Form or `useState`), a draft-based `dirty`, and an `OwnDiscardQuestion` whose file has no guard reading an unsaved state, and no exception marker waives these findings. Details: [unsaved changes in an overlay](references/frontend/references/overlay.md#25-beforeclose-checks-before-closing).

Use [the frontend workflow](references/frontend/ui-workflow.md) selected during feature planning, or select it before a frontend-only change. Routine pages and CRUD using established patterns take the quick workflow; complex interactions and cross-module design decisions take the full workflow with internal design and acceptance reviews. Theme changes use their own verification. Each workflow routes to the relevant [UI guidelines](references/frontend/ui-guidelines.md) and [frontend handbook](references/frontend/frontend-dev.md); none adds a default user approval round.

The handbook's "Look up by task" table routes each frontend task to the sections that cover it, and [the worked example](references/frontend/references/example.md) holds the complete files of the projects feature its rules are illustrated with. Components are shadcn/ui primitives, added with the CLI when a page first needs one: the shadcn/ui skill in `references/frontend/shadcn/` covers their API and composition rules, and [its guide in this handbook](references/frontend/references/shadcn.md) says what to read there and where this application departs from it.

## Choose your reference

Read the page for the task in front of you. Do not read all of them.

| Task                                                                                                                              | Read                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Anything under `client/`: pages, routes, components, styling, forms, API calls, copy, frontend tests                              | [frontend workflow](references/frontend/ui-workflow.md), which routes to the [frontend handbook](references/frontend/frontend-dev.md), the theme reference or the worked example                                                                                                                                                     |
| How a page works on a phone: first screen, lists as cards, filters, tabs, forms, overlays, touch, phone verification              | [phone experience](references/frontend/mobile.md)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Search/paginate relation choices, save associations, or batch-assign selected records                                             | [executable relation and batch example](references/frontend/references/executable-relation-batch.md), then the installed authorization Skill                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Add an API endpoint, a webhook, or a callback; authenticate and authorize it                                                      | [server routes](references/server-routes.md)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Name an endpoint, shape its response or errors, validate its input, paginate a list, document it in the API document              | [HTTP API design](references/http-api.md)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| A list, chart or polled endpoint, or keeping one live: read it with a fixed number of queries, refresh only what changed          | [server routes](references/server-routes.md#lists-and-statistics-a-fixed-number-of-queries) and [client API requests](references/frontend/references/api.md#keeping-lists-and-charts-live)                                                                                                                                           |
| Query or write data, resolve the database, work with transactions                                                                 | [database and data access](references/database-and-data.md)

--- name: shadcn description: Manages shadcn components and projects — adding, searching, fixing, debugging, styling, and composing UI, including chat interfaces. Provides project context, component docs, and usage examples. Applies when working with shadcn/ui, component registries, presets, --preset codes, or any project with a components.json file. Also triggers for "shadcn init", "create an app with --preset", or "switch to --preset". user-invocable: false allowed-tools: Bash(npx shadcn@latest *), Bash(pnpm dlx shadcn@latest *), Bash(bunx --bun shadcn@latest *) --- # shadcn/ui A framework for building ui, components and design systems. Components are added as source code to the user's project via the CLI. > **IMPORTANT:** Run all CLI commands using the project's package runner: `npx shadcn@latest`, `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest`, or `bunx --bun shadcn@latest` — based on the project's `packageManager`. Examples below use `npx shadcn@latest` but substitute the correct runner for the project. ## Current Project Context ```json !`npx shadcn@latest info --json` ``` The JSON above contains the project config and installed components. Use `npx shadcn@latest docs ` to get documentation and example URLs for any component. ## Principles 1. **Use existing components first.** Use `npx shadcn@latest search` to check registries before writing custom UI. Check community registries too. 2. **Compose, don't reinvent.** Settings page = Tabs + Card + form controls. Dashboard = Sidebar + Card + Chart + Table. 3. **Use built-in variants before custom styles.** `variant="outline"`, `size="sm"`, etc. 4. **Use semantic colors.** `bg-primary`, `text-muted-foreground` — never raw values like `bg-blue-500`. ## Critical Rules These rules are **always enforced**. Each links to a file with Incorrect/Correct code pairs. ### Styling & Tailwind → [styling.md](./rules/styling.md) - **`className` for layout, not styling.** Never override component colors or typography. - **No `space-x-*` or `space-y-*`.** Use `flex` with `gap-*`. For vertical stacks, `flex flex-col gap-*`. - **Use `size-*` when width and height are equal.** `size-10` not `w-10 h-10`. - **Use `truncate` shorthand.** Not `overflow-hidden text-ellipsis whitespace-nowrap`. - **No manual `dark:` color overrides.** Use semantic tokens (`bg-background`, `text-muted-foreground`). - **Use `cn()` for conditional classes.** Don't write manual template literal ternaries. - **No manual `z-index` on overlay components.** Dialog, Sheet, Popover, etc. handle their own stacking. ### Forms & Inputs → [forms.md](./rules/forms.md) - **Forms use `FieldGroup` + `Field`.** Never use raw `div` with `space-y-*` or `grid gap-*` for form layout. - **`InputGroup` uses `InputGroupInput`/`InputGroupTextarea`.** Never raw `Input`/`Textarea` inside `InputGroup`. - **Buttons inside inputs use `InputGroup` + `InputGroupAddon`.** - **Option sets (2–7 choices) use `ToggleGroup`.** Don't loop `Button` with manual active state. - **`FieldSet` + `FieldLegend` for grouping related checkboxes/radios.** Don't use a `div` with a heading. - **Field validation uses `data-invalid` + `aria-invalid`.** `data-invalid` on `Field`, `aria-invalid` on the control. For disabled: `data-disabled` on `Field`, `disabled` on the control. ### Component Structure → [composition.md](./rules/composition.md) - **Items always inside their Group.** `SelectItem` → `SelectGroup`. `DropdownMenuItem` → `DropdownMenuGroup`. `CommandItem` → `CommandGroup`. - **Use `asChild` (radix) or `render` (base) for custom triggers.** Check `base` field from `npx shadcn@latest info`. → [base-vs-radix.md](./rules/base-vs-radix.md) - **Dialog, Sheet, and Drawer always need a Title.** `DialogTitle`, `SheetTitle`, `DrawerTitle` required for accessibility. Use `className="sr-only"` if visually hidden. - **Use full Card composition.** `CardHeader`/`CardTitle`/`CardDescription`/`CardContent`/`CardFooter`. Don't dump everything in `CardContent`. - **Button has no `isPending`/`isLoading`.** Compose with `Spinner` + `data-icon` + `disabled`. - **`TabsTrigger` must be inside `TabsList`.** Never render triggers directly in `Tabs`. - **`Avatar` always needs `AvatarFallback`.** For when the image fails to load. ### Use Components, Not Custom Markup → [composition.md](./rules/composition.md) - **Use existing components before custom markup.** Check if a component exists before writing a styled `div`. - **Callouts use `Alert`.** Don't build custom styled divs. - **Empty states use `Empty`.** Don't build custom empty state markup. - **Toast follows the project base.** Use `toast` from the `toast` component for Base UI projects. Use `toast()` from `sonner` for Radix and React Aria projects. - **Use `Separator`** instead of `
` or `
`. - **Use `Skeleton`** for loading placeholders. No custom `animate-pulse` divs. - **Use `Badge`** instead of custom styled spans. ### Icons → [icons.md](./rules/icons.md) - **Icons in `Button` use `data-icon`.** `data-icon="inline-start"` or `data-icon="inline-end"` on the icon. - **No sizing classes on icons inside components.** Components handle icon sizing via CSS. No `size-4` or `w-4 h-4`. - **Pass icons as objects, not string keys.** `icon={CheckIcon}`, not a string lookup. ### Chat & Messaging → [chat.md](./rules/chat.md) - **Chat UI composes the chat primitives.** Conversations use `MessageScroller`, rows use `Message`, surfaces use `Bubble`. Never hand-rolled bubble `div`s or a raw scroll container. - **`MessageScroller` owns scroll behavior.** Streaming follow, anchoring, and jump-to-latest (`MessageScrollerButton`) are built in. Don't write a `useStickToBottom`/`ResizeObserver` hook. - **Attachments use `Attachment`; system notes and dividers use `Marker`.** Not `Item` cards or `Separator` + a label. ### CLI - **Never decode preset codes or build preset URLs manually.** Use `npx shadcn@latest preset decode `, `preset url `, or `preset open `. For project-aware preset detection, use `npx shadcn@latest preset resolve`. - **Apply preset codes directly with the CLI.** Use `npx shadcn@latest apply ` for existing projects, or `npx shadcn@latest init --preset ` when initializing. ## Key Patterns These are the most common patterns that differentiate correct shadcn/ui code. For edge cases, see the linked rule files above. ```tsx // Form layout: FieldGroup + Field, not div + Label. Email // Validation: data-invalid on Field, aria-invalid on the control. Email Invalid email. // Icons in buttons: data-icon, no sizing classes. // Spacing: gap-*, not space-y-*.
// correct
// wrong // Equal dimensions: size-*, not w-* h-*. // correct // wrong // Status colors: Badge variants or semantic tokens, not raw colors. +20.1% // correct +20.1% // wrong ``` ## Component Selection | Need | Use | | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Button/action | `Button` with appropriate variant | | Form inputs | `Input`, `Select`, `Combobox`, `Switch`, `Checkbox`, `RadioGroup`, `Textarea`, `InputOTP`, `Slider` | | Toggle between 2–5 options | `ToggleGroup` + `ToggleGroupItem` | | Data display | `Table`, `Card`, `Badge`, `Avatar` | | Navigation | `Sidebar`, `NavigationMenu`, `Breadcrumb`, `Tabs`, `Pagination` | | Overlays | `Dialog` (modal), `Sheet` (side panel), `Drawer` (bottom sheet), `AlertDialog` (confirmation) | | Feedback | `toast` (Base UI), `sonner` (Radix/Aria), `Alert`, `Progress`, `Skeleton`, `Spinner` | | Command palette | `Command` inside `Dialog` | | Charts | `Chart` (wraps Recharts) | | Layout | `Card`, `Separator`, `Resizable`, `ScrollArea`, `Accordion`, `Collapsible` | | Empty states | `Empty` | | Menus | `DropdownMenu`, `ContextMenu`, `Menubar` | | Tooltips/info | `Tooltip`, `HoverCard`, `Popover` | | Chat / conversation UI | `MessageScroller`, `Message`, `Bubble`, `Attachment`, `Marker` | ## Key Fields The injected project context contains these key fields: - **`aliases`** → use the actual alias prefix for imports (e.g. `@/`, `~/`), never hardcode. - **`isRSC`** → when `true`, components using `useState`, `useEffect`, event handlers, or browser APIs need `"use client"` at the top of the file. Always reference this field when advising on the directive. - **`tailwindVersion`** → `"v4"` uses `@theme inline` blocks; `"v3"` uses `tailwind.config.js`. - **`tailwindCssFile`** → the global CSS file where custom CSS variables are defined. Always edit this file, never create a new one. - **`style`** → component visual treatment (e.g. `nova`, `vega`). - **`base`** → primitive library (`radix` or `base`). Affects component APIs and available props. - **`iconLibrary`** → determines icon imports. Use `lucide-react` for `lucide`, `@tabler/icons-react` for `tabler`, etc. Never assume `lucide-react`. - **`resolvedPaths`** → exact file-system destinations for components, utils, hooks, etc. - **`framework`** → routing and file conventions (e.g. Next.js App Router vs Vite SPA). - **`packageManager`** → use this for any non-shadcn dependency installs (e.g. `pnpm add date-fns` vs `npm install date-fns`). - **`preset`** → resolved preset code and values for the current project. Use `npx shadcn@latest preset resolve --json` when you only need preset information. See [cli.md — `info` command](./cli.md) for the full field reference. ## Component Docs, Examples, and Usage Run `npx shadcn@latest docs ` to get the URLs for a component's documentation, examples, and API reference. Fetch these URLs to get the actual content. ```bash npx shadcn@latest docs button dialog select ``` **When creating, fixing, debugging, or using a component, always run `npx shadcn@latest docs` and fetch the URLs first.** This ensures you're working with the correct API and usage patterns rather than guessing. ## Workflow 1. **Get project context** — already injected above. Run `npx shadcn@latest info` again if you need to refresh. 2. **Check installed components first** — before running `add`, always check the `components` list from project context or list the `resolvedPaths.ui` directory. Don't import components that haven't been added, and don't re-add ones already installed. 3. **Find components** — `npx shadcn@latest search`. 4. **Get docs and examples** — run `npx shadcn@latest docs ` to get URLs, then fetch them. Use `npx shadcn@latest view` to browse registry items you haven't installed. To preview changes to installed components, use `npx shadcn@latest add --diff`. 5. **Install or update** — `npx shadcn@latest add`. When updating existing components, use `--dry-run` and `--diff` to preview changes first (see [Updating Components](#updating-components) below). 6. **Fix imports in third-party components** — After adding components from community registries (e.g. `@bundui`, `@magicui`), check the added non-UI files for hardcoded import paths like `@/components/ui/...`. These won't match the project's actual aliases. Use `npx shadcn@latest info` to get the correct `ui` alias (e.g. `@workspace/ui/components`) and rewrite the imports accordingly. The CLI rewrites imports for its own UI files, but third-party registry components may use default paths that don't match the project. 7. **Review added components** — After adding a component or block from any registry, **always read the added files and verify they are correct**. Check for missing sub-components (e.g. `SelectItem` without `SelectGroup`), missing imports, incorrect composition, or violations of the [Critical Rules](#critical-rules). Also replace any icon imports with the project's `iconLibrary` from the project context (e.g. if the registry item uses `lucide-react` but the project uses `hugeicons`, swap the imports and icon names accordingly). Fix all issues before moving on. 8. **Registry must be explicit** — When the user asks to add a block or component, **do not guess the registry**. If no registry is specified (e.g. user says "add a login block" without specifying `@shadcn`, `@tailark`, `owner/repo`, etc.), ask which registry to use. Never default to a registry on behalf of the user. 9. **Switching presets** — Ask the user first: **overwrite**, **partial**, **merge**, or **skip**? - **Inspect current preset**: `npx shadcn@latest preset resolve`. Use `--json` when you need structured values. - **Inspect incoming preset**: `npx shadcn@latest preset decode `. Use `preset url ` or `preset open ` to share or open the preset builder. - **Overwrite**: `npx shadcn@latest apply `. Overwrites detected components, fonts, and CSS variables. - **Partial**: `npx shadcn@latest apply --only theme,font`. Updates only the selected preset parts without reinstalling UI components. Supported values are `theme` and `font`; comma-separated combinations are allowed. `icon` is intentionally not supported, because icon changes may require full component reinstall and transforms. - **Merge**: `npx shadcn@latest init --preset --force --no-reinstall`, then run `npx shadcn@latest info` to list installed components, then for each installed component use `--dry-run` and `--diff` to [smart merge](#updating-components) it individually. - **Skip**: `npx shadcn@latest init --preset --force --no-reinstall`. Only updates config and CSS, leaves components as-is. - **Important**: Always run preset commands inside the user's project directory. `apply` only works in an existing project with a `components.json` file. The CLI automatically preserves the current base (`base` vs `radix`) from `components.json`. If you must use a scratch/temp directory (e.g. for `--dry-run` comparisons), pass `--base ` explicitly — preset codes do not encode the base. ## Updating Components When the user asks to update a component from upstream while keeping their local changes, use `--dry-run` and `--diff` to intelligently merge. **NEVER fetch raw files from GitHub manually — always use the CLI.** 1. Run `npx shadcn@latest add --dry-run` to see all files that would be affected. 2. For each file, run `npx shadcn@latest add --diff ` to see what changed upstream vs local. 3. Decide per file based on the diff: - No local changes → safe to overwrite. - Has local changes → read the local file, analyze the diff, and apply upstream updates while preserving local modifications. - User says "just update everything" → use `--overwrite`, but confirm first. 4. **Never use `--overwrite` without the user's explicit approval.** ## Quick Reference ```bash # Create a new project. npx shadcn@latest init --name my-app --preset base-nova npx shadcn@latest init --name my-app --preset a2r6bw --template vite # Create a monorepo project. npx shadcn@latest init --name my-app --preset base-nova --monorepo npx shadcn@latest init --name my-app --preset base-nova --template next --monorepo # Initialize existing project. npx shadcn@latest init --preset base-nova npx shadcn@latest init --defaults # shortcut: --template=next --preset=nova (base style implied) # Apply a preset to an existing project. npx shadcn@latest apply a2r6bw npx shadcn@latest apply a2r6bw --only theme npx shadcn@latest apply a2r6bw --only font npx shadcn@latest apply a2r6bw --only theme,font # Inspect preset codes and project preset state. npx shadcn@latest preset decode a2r6bw npx shadcn@latest preset url a2r6bw npx shadcn@latest preset open a2r6bw npx shadcn@latest preset resolve npx shadcn@latest preset resolve --json # Add components. npx shadcn@latest add button card dialog npx shadcn@latest add @magicui/shimmer-button npx shadcn@latest add owner/repo/item npx shadcn@latest add --all # Preview changes before adding/updating. npx shadcn@latest add button --dry-run npx shadcn@latest add button --diff button.tsx npx shadcn@latest add @acme/form --view button.tsx npx shadcn@latest add owner/repo/item --dry-run # Search registries. npx shadcn@latest search @shadcn -q "sidebar" npx shadcn@latest search @tailark -q "stats" npx shadcn@latest search owner/repo -q "login" npx shadcn@latest search # all configured registries npx shadcn@latest search @shadcn -q "menu" -t ui # filter by item type # Get component docs and example URLs. npx shadcn@latest docs button dialog select # View registry item details (for items not yet installed). npx shadcn@latest view @shadcn/button npx shadcn@latest view owner/repo/item ``` **Named presets:** `nova`, `vega`, `maia`, `lyra`, `mira`, `luma` **Templates:** `next`, `vite`, `start`, `react-router`, `astro` (all support `--monorepo`) and `laravel` (not supported for monorepo) **Preset codes:** Version-prefixed base62 strings (e.g. `a2r6bw` or `b0`), from [ui.shadcn.com](https://ui.shadcn.com). ## Detailed References - [rules/forms.md](./rules/forms.md) — FieldGroup, Field, InputGroup, ToggleGroup, FieldSet, validation states - [rules/composition.md](./rules/composition.md) — Groups, overlays, Card, Tabs, Avatar, Alert, Empty, Toast, Separator, Skeleton, Badge, Button loading - [rules/chat.md](./rules/chat.md) — MessageScroller, Message, Bubble, Attachment, Marker; streaming, anchoring, jump-to-latest - [rules/icons.md](./rules/icons.md) — data-icon, icon sizing, passing icons as objects - [rules/styling.md](./rules/styling.md) — Semantic colors, variants, className, spacing, size, truncate, dark mode, cn(), z-index - [rules/base-vs-radix.md](./rules/base-vs-radix.md) — asChild vs render, Select, ToggleGroup, Slider, Accordion - [cli.md](./cli.md) — Commands, flags, presets, templates - [registry.md](./registry.md) — Authoring source registries, `include`, item definitions, dependencies, GitHub registry rules - [customization.md](./customization.md) — Theming, CSS variables, extending components

skills.content:
---
name: nocobase-app-plugin-development
description: Create and maintain NocoBase 3 plugins inside an existing App or a NocoBase 3 source workspace, including Client, Server, CLI, database resources, UI Library integration, Plugin Skills, and registration. Use for App-local plugins under packages/ and source-workspace plugins or examples. Not for creating an App, application-only feature work, or legacy NocoBase 2 plugins.
---

# NocoBase Plugin Development

Use this Skill to develop a plugin in the user’s existing NocoBase 3 App. Read that App’s `AGENTS.md`, relevant installed Skills, and the plugin before editing. An App created by create-app identifies itself with `nocobase.templateKind: "app"` in `package.json`; its local plugins belong in `packages/`. Start from an installed App with working dependencies. If no App exists, use the available `nocobase-create-app` Skill first, then return here. Do not download the NocoBase source repository as a prerequisite.

This Skill ships with the App's installed `@nocobase/app-skills`; update it through a compatible App upgrade and `pnpm nocobase skills sync`, not by editing the generated copy or installing a global copy. Read it by its project path when an older global entry has the same name. The upgrade Skill describes retiring that global installation after a project replacement is verified.

For work explicitly in the NocoBase source repository, the repository links this same maintained Skill locally. Read `.agents/rules/plugin-development.md` from that repository root for source-only creation, registration and validation commands. An App does not need those repository files. Source paths in references are optional lookup locations; use installed exports, declarations and synchronized Skills to verify APIs for the App's version. Do not apply the legacy `Plugin` class, `src/client-v2/` or `nb scaffold plugin` protocol. If the creation tool or App CLI lacks App-workspace support, report the incompatible packages instead of hand-building a scaffold or downloading the source repository.

## Choose the relevant references

These English references adapt the plugin development guide into task-specific instructions. Read the rows relevant to the task; do not load the entire reference set by default.

| Task                                                                                                  | Read                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Create a plugin, choose capabilities, change declarations, exports, dependencies, or public contracts | [Scaffolding and package contracts](references/plugin-foundation.md) |
| Register, configure, upgrade, disable, unregister, or diagnose plugin integration                     | [Registration and lifecycle](references/registration.md)             |
| Choose Client components, ServiceProviders, React Providers, configuration, or API access             | [Client architecture](references/client.md)                          |
| Define Server configuration defaults, environment mappings, validation, or browser-visible fields    | [Plugin configuration](references/configuration.md)                  |
| Migrate Concurrency, Jobs or Queue backend selectors and existing application factories | [Strict backend configuration](references/backends-configuration.md) |
| Build or change any plugin UI                                                                         | [Shared UI design and host acceptance](references/ui-design.md), then [shadcn components and styling](references/client-components.md) |
| Add business pages, menus, Tabs, route dialogs/drawers, child routes, or page overrides                 | [Client routing](references/client-routing.md)                       |
| Design configuration entities, settings permissions, routed editors and safe saves                    | [System settings](references/system-settings.md)                     |
| Define service contracts, Tokens, dependency injection, or lifecycle                                  | [Services and Providers](references/services.md)                     |
| Add HTTP endpoints, authorization, Repository operations, background jobs, or queues                  | [Server development](references/server.md)                           |
| Name an `/api` path, choose its method, shape its response or error, or validate its input            | [HTTP API rules](references/http-api.md)                             |
| Add migrations, seeds, or package resource/checksum handling                                          | [Database resources](references/database.md)                         |
| Add or change text, locale resources, translated errors, or recipient-language messages               | [Internationalization](references/i18n.md)                           |
| Author, publish, install, upgrade, or remove App-owned editable Client source                         | [UI Library ownership](references/registry.md)                                   |
| Expose a plugin's capabilities to the App Agent                                                       | [Plugin Skills](references/plugin-skills.md)                         |
| Add commands, CLI exports, or CLI registration                                                        | [CLI plugins](references/cli.md)                                     |
| Use `@nocobase/app-testing` for database, Server, Client or CLI tests and verify App integration       | [Testing and delivery](references/testing.md)                        |
| Follow one executable plugin through migrations, protected API, Client, configuration and CLI tests | [Complete testing example](references/testing-example.md)            |

For Realtime changes, check whether the target workspace or application provides a version-matched `nocobase-realtime` Skill from `@nocobase/realtime`; read it alongside the installed API declarations. Package integration guidance must match the target runtime version.

For worked implementations and tests, read the matching [Server Route examples](references/server-route-examples.md), [ServiceToken and Provider examples](references/service-examples.md), [Client examples](references/client-examples.md), or [Repository examples](references/repository-examples.md). These supplement the topic references with concrete code and point to maintained source fixtures; adapt their explicit example access policies to the requested product.

## Rules that apply before implementation

For UI work, first read [the shared UI design entry](references/ui-design.md): it locates the same design contract, reference modes, authorized exceptions and acceptance rules used by application development. Read the host's design decisions before choosing a layout, retain approved decisions outside synchronized Skills, and verify the rendered plugin in the host. Package ownership and implementation remain governed by this Skill.

When creating a page or writing a page component, refer to [Pages, routes, and menus](references/client-pages-and-routes.md) for page component structure and route declarations. For nested pages, page-level navigation Tabs, route dialogs/drawers, or navigation groups, also read [Child routes, Tabs, overlays, navigation groups, and Outlet](references/client-child-routes.md). Before using the page and overlay examples, [copy the required component source into the plugin](references/client-components.md#copy-page-and-route-components-into-the-plugin). The examples import these plugin-owned copies through relative `.js` paths; the host's private breadcrumb component is excluded. For route overlay component availability and hook context boundaries, read [route dialogs and drawers](references/client-routing.md#route-dialogs-and-drawers).

- Follow the shared component selection order: existing plugin/public business component → installed plugin-owned shadcn primitive → registry addition → justified custom implementation. Record source imports and underlying primitives, review custom gaps, and run the targeted checker as [the UI entry](references/ui-design.md) describes.
- Use shadcn components for interactive UI primitives such as buttons, inputs, dialogs, selects, and Tabs. Read the component reference before UI work. Keep plugin-owned components in the plugin and align `components.json` with its package-local `#` imports and published `dist` mappings. Use the shared theme tokens for color, typography, spacing, size, radius, and shadow.
- Use child routes for page-level navigation Tabs by default, even when the user does not mention routing. Declare each Tab's content as a child route, render `Outlet` in the parent page component, and derive the active Tab from the URL. When the parent URL is opened without a child route, redirect to the default accessible Tab by replacing the current history entry and preserving query parameters. Opening an explicit Tab URL must retain that Tab's selection. Follow an explicit user request for a different interaction.
- In an existing App, create plugins with `pnpm create @nocobase/plugin@beta` and explicit capabilities, including `cli` when needed. In a source checkout, follow its repository-local creation instructions. Preview with `--dry-run --json`, check the target and project edits, then apply the same capability selection. Keep the generated runtime-aware shared development configuration; see [scaffolding](references/plugin-foundation.md).
- Keep declarations static and free of startup side effects. Lazy-load page components, locale messages, heavy SDKs, and genuinely optional features at their leaf boundaries. Pages are Routes, components are public/source exports, and neither is a separate runtime loader.
- Translate all plugin copy into the ten [supported languages](references/i18n.md#ship-all-ten-supported-languages) (`en-US`, `zh-CN`, `zh-TW`, `ja-JP`, `es-ES`, `pt-BR`, `fr-FR`, `de-DE`, `vi-VN`, `id-ID`) in every Client and Server locale manifest, typed with the complete `en-US` resource. Libraries the plugin depends on that ship translations, such as `@nocobase/i18n` for `@nocobase/app-plugin-i18n`, are completed to all ten as well. A new or changed key is translated into all ten in the same change; application templates are exempt.
- Reuse the host's API client through `useApiClient()` or `apiClientToken`; do not construct another application API client. Define shared service contracts and owner-created Tokens before implementations; consumers import the original Token.
- A plugin contributes no settings or dev pages; `defineAppRoutes()` is the only Client route API. Expose administration as settings items and APIs, grouped by management area (for example, Automation contains Workflow and Schedules), and leave any page over them to the application. See [System settings](references/system-settings.md) for declarations and server operation boundaries.
- Every `/api` route follows the [HTTP API rules](references/http-api.md): camelCase paths under the plugin's namespace, standard methods, `{ data }` responses, `ApiError` for every failure (clients branch on `reason`), zod input validated through `apiValidator()`, and a `describeRoute()` declaration on every route for the application's OpenAPI document at `/api/swagger/docs`. Data endpoints are `POST /api/{name}/{action}` with camelCase exposure names and are documented without a declaration.
- Each Server Route owns and tests its authentication and authorization, or its explicit public protocol boundary. Another contribution's middleware or registration order is not protection. Test the production contribution through `createRouter()`.
- Every Server plugin declares an absolute `baseDir`. Migrations, seeds, and Jobs resolve relative to it so compiled plugins use compiled resources. Migrations are explicit, self-contained, immutable after merge, and tested against a real database.
- Plugin test fixtures come from `@nocobase/app-testing/server`, `/client` or `/cli`, declared in `devDependencies`. Use the [test directory and fixture guide](references/testing.md#use-app-testing-in-a-plugin) to select the environment, register the production plugin and keep databases and storage isolated.
- Register Client, Server, and CLI exports explicitly in the corresponding target App composition roots. Installation, registration, Skills synchronization, and runtime behavior are separate facts; legacy manifest metadata is not runtime discovery.
- Plugin integration knowledge is authored in `<plugin>/skills/`; the target App's `.agents/skills/` is generated output. Editable UI is maintained in the UI Library; source installed into an App belongs to that App. This development Skill is maintained in `@nocobase/app-skills`, distinct from a plugin's own integration Skills.
- Follow the target project’s dependency rules: shared runtimes and client value imports are peers, ordinary server runtime imports are dependencies, and development-only imports are devDependencies. A type reference retained in published declarations needs a consumer-resolvable contract.

## Implementation workflow

1. Inspect working-tree changes, plugin manifests, declarations, exports, tests, and the target App. Identify the requested behavior and who owns its data, UI, services, and integration code.
2. Select capabilities and define the smallest public contracts: Client options/exports, Server Tokens/APIs, CLI commands, permission/error boundaries, and observable results. Use only the relevant references above.
3. Implement in the owning plugin. Put domain behavior in Services, HTTP boundaries in Routes, asynchronous orchestration in Jobs, React context in React Providers, and application integration instructions in Plugin Skills.
4. Keep declarations, source/publish exports, dependencies, published files, tests, README, and Plugin Skills consistent. Remove unused scaffold examples and drafts. Write each Markdown prose paragraph on one physical line, without manual line wrapping.
5. When integration is part of the request, preview and apply registration to the chosen App, synchronize applicable Skills, and validate the resulting behavior. Do not run creation, registration, migration, or other stateful commands merely because this Skill applies.
6. Follow [testing and delivery](references/testing.md): run the modified plugin's checks and relevant consumer checks, then verify the requested runtime workflow. `plugin inspect` is an optional read-only registration diagnostic, not a test or completion gate. Report results, skipped checks, and remaining limitations accurately.
